name: security-mysql-account-grants-review
intent: MySQL effective account/host matching and stored-object privileges
artifacts: Server version, matched user/host account, role activation, grants and definer/invoker objects.
trace: Resolve the actual authenticated account and effective active roles before following a stored routine/view into protected tables.
experiment: Use an isolated database with two owned users and synthetic rows; compare intended access and a controlled definer-object invocation.
disproof: A broad grant on a different host account or inactive role is not effective access for the tested connection.
repair: Constrain matched account and stored-object authority, testing normal routines and restricted table operations.
branch_decisions: Resolve the matched user@host account, active roles and direct grants before invoking stored-object authority. SQL SECURITY DEFINER may deliberately delegate a narrow operation; inspect definer identity, object body and caller-controlled arguments only when that path is reachable. A client-supplied username alone does not identify the effective server account.
